title: Juniper and the Choir
premise: Casper Kavanagh has spent nine years hiding her beast-speaker gift behind the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, a trade house that deals in impossible things—bottled storms, borrowed years, names sold at auction. When Juniper, a mute child who speaks only in a language older than any kingdom, is left at the guild's door, Casper realizes the girl's tongue is the key to a door out of a country that was erased from maps and memory two centuries ago. The Guild's masters want Juniper as inventory; the country's exiled dead want her as a vessel; and Casper's own gift, long suppressed, begins answering voices she never invited. To save the child, Casper must unlearn her invisibility, bargain with the thing that erased the country, and pay the price of survival she has dodged all her life: being seen. In the end she opens the door—not to escape it, but to let what remains of the vanished country finally pass through—and chooses exile over silence, carrying Juniper into a world where both of them can be heard.
about_author: Ansel Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing defunct guild records in coastal port cities. Their fiction blends bureaucratic precision with folkloric dread, and 'Juniper and the Choir' is their second novel.

chapters.title: The Weight of Quiet Things
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A day in the Vellum Guild: Casper audits a crate of bottled thunderstorms while suppressing the whispers of the guild's caged messenger-moths, who beg her in their small voices. Establishes her invisibility as armor. Emotional beat: loneliness mistaken for safety.

chapters.title: A Knock Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A dying woman leaves a silent child on the guild steps; the child writes symbols no scribe recognizes. When Casper touches the doorframe, every animal within a mile goes still. Emotional beat: dread—the first crack in Casper's careful life.

chapters.title: Inventory
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Oren Vetch's POV. Vetch classifies the child, Juniper, as an acquisition, not an orphan, and orders her held for appraisal. He notices Casper lingering too long near the holding room. Emotional beat: cold institutional menace.

chapters.title: What the Moths Know
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The messenger-moths tell Casper that Juniper's language isn't unknown—it's remembered, by things that were alive before kingdoms. Casper answers one moth aloud for the first time in years. Emotional beat: terror and longing entwined.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV (fragmentary, sensory). Juniper endures the guild's testing—mirrors, blood-ink, a name-eater worm—and refuses to speak, protecting something inside herself. She marks Casper as different from the others. Emotional beat: fierce, quiet resistance.

chapters.title: Ledgers of the Vanished
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Digging in the guild's forbidden archive, Casper finds a ledger from a country called Serevan—struck from every map 200 years ago—with entries matching Juniper's symbols exactly. Emotional beat: vertigo; history is not what she was told.

chapters.title: The Choir in the Walls
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. At night, Casper hears singing under the floorboards—voices of Serevan's exiled dead, sealed beneath the guild when it was built on their capital's ruin. They call Juniper 'the last mouth.' Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Terms of Sale
chapters.summary: Vetch's POV. A buyer arrives: the Pale Assessor, an agent of the Crown's Bureau of Erasure, offering a fortune for anything Serevan-touched. Vetch agrees to sell Juniper within the week. Emotional beat: greed dressed as prudence.

chapters.title: Small Treasons
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper smuggles food and paper to Juniper; the girl draws a door, then draws Casper standing before it. Casper's suppressed gift surges—she understands a full sentence of the old tongue without trying. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: The Beast-Speaker's Bargain
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The guild's oldest resident, a blind cellar-cat named Hesper who is far more than a cat, reveals she knew Casper's grandmother—a Serevan speaker who paid a price to hide her line. Hesper offers training if Casper accepts the cost. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: Lessons in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Through Hesper and Juniper together, Casper learns the basics of Serevan speech and its rule: every word spoken is a piece of the speaker given away. Her first true sentence costs her a memory of her mother's face. Emotional beat: grief as tuition.

chapters.title: What the Bureau Burns
chapters.summary: Bureau clerk Imre Sol's POV. Sol, sent to verify the purchase, burns a village's memory-records and feels nothing—until he glimpses Juniper and hears, faintly, the choir. Emotional beat: a functionary's first doubt.

chapters.title: The Night of Open Cages
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper frees the guild's beasts to create chaos and steals Juniper from the holding room—but Vetch anticipated her, and the escape fails. Hesper buys their lives by revealing herself to Vetch, and is taken instead. Emotional beat: guilt and fury.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Cat
chapters.summary: Vetch's POV. Vetch bargains with Hesper, learning that Casper is a beast-speaker of Serevan descent—the most valuable asset the guild has ever possessed. His ambition turns from profit to possession. Emotional beat: corruption finding its shape.

chapters.title: The Price Already Paid
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Hunted within the guild's walls, Casper learns from the choir why Serevan was erased: its speakers refused to sell their language to the first Bureau, so the Bureau unmade the country rather than fail to own it. Emotional beat: understanding the enemy.

chapters.title: Sol's Choice
chapters.summary: Imre Sol's POV. Ordered to take Juniper early, Sol instead falsifies his report and seeks out Casper, offering Bureau seals and routes in exchange for a chance to hear the choir himself. Emotional beat: defection born of hunger, not virtue.

chapters.title: The Door Beneath the Ledger Hall
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Guided by Juniper's drawings and the choir's song, Casper, Juniper, and Sol find the sealed Serevan door beneath the guild—but Vetch and Bureau enforcers arrive, Hesper captive, demanding Casper open it for them. Emotional beat: cornered resolve.

chapters.title: Every Word a Wound
chapters.summary: Climax, Casper's POV. Casper speaks Serevan aloud—giving away memory after memory—to command the door, while Vetch tries to seize Juniper as a vessel and Sol turns his own Bureau tools against the enforcers. Hesper breaks free and holds the line. Emotional beat: sacrifice made visible.

chapters.title: What Passes Through
chapters.summary: Climax continues, Juniper's POV. The door opens onto Serevan's remnant: not a place but a chorus awaiting a mouth. Juniper, revealed as the country's final speaker, chooses to give the dead their words back rather than become their container—and the choir, released, dissolves into light. Emotional beat: release after long captivity.

chapters.title: The Cost of Being Seen
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Vetch, having touched the open door, is unmade by everything he tried to own; the Bureau's claim collapses with Sol's testimony. Casper, nearly emptied of memory, cannot stay—her gift is now known, and known things get owned. Emotional beat: bittersweet victory.

chapters.title: Exile, Chosen
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper and Juniper leave the city at dawn with Hesper, carrying a new blank ledger. Casper begins re-teaching herself Serevan, accepting that each word costs, and that some things are worth the price. Emotional beat: quiet hope.

chapters.title: The First Word
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating Casper and Juniper. On a road beyond the maps, Juniper speaks her first word aloud in months—Casper's name, in the old tongue. Casper answers in kind, paying gladly. Somewhere behind them, a new choir begins. Emotional beat: voice found, inheritance transformed into gift.
